The bag of Shell Coins was heavy, many of them in denominations of a thousand. Ming An raised an eyebrow, running his fingers over them before chuckling.

The footsteps behind him grew louder. The door swung open again as the guard captain, Ying Liancang, entered with his men, shaking his head. “The Empress gave you a chance to redeem yourself.”

“I have committed no crime. There is nothing to redeem.”

“Twice now, you’ve allowed a fugitive to escape. Even with over a decade of kinship between us, I can’t save you this time.”

Still smiling, Ming An weighed the bag in his hand before passing it to Ying Liancang. “After working together for so many years, surely burying me once isn’t too much to ask?”

“…” Ying Liancang accepted the pouch, lowering his gaze.

His men rushed past him in pursuit of Mingyi, their movements thunderous. Only then did he raise his blade, resting it horizontally above Ming An’s head.

Mingyi ran without looking back. Xiuyun was too slow, so she carried her on her back, intermittently riding her sword when her Essence Power allowed. When it ran low, she sprinted on foot, resting briefly before taking to the sword again. This way, they managed to stay ahead of their pursuers.

Xiuyun, jostled breathless, finally found her voice once they steadied on the sword. “That man was so kind. The way he looked at you just now—it was like… like you were some kind of treasure.”

Mingyi froze, her speed faltering abruptly.

She rarely saw Ming An and had never really interacted with him. In her memory, every time her mother came to check on her training progress, Ming An would stand in the distance, hands clasped, glancing over briefly.

Far from being kind, he had barely spoken to her in over a decade. So why had someone like him just shown such emotion moments ago?

CONTENT END 124

chapters.title: Chapter 125
chapters.content:
“That’s not right.” Mingyi suddenly stopped in her tracks as realization dawned. “If the Empress knew I was alive, she wouldn’t have sent him to find me.”

Having already spared her once, why would she give him the chance to do it again? Unless… the Empress was doing this deliberately. She wanted to prove something.

A chill ran down Mingyi’s spine. Gritting her teeth, she suddenly broke into a sprint toward the competition grounds outside the city.

Going back now wouldn’t save Ming An—it would only mean certain death. Unless Ji Bozhai came to her aid.

She needed Ji Bozhai.

At the competition grounds, the matches were already halfway through, with exceptionally fierce battles underway. All the teams that had been relatively easy to handle yesterday had switched out their members today.

The Star Yearn City team, already at a disadvantage without their Artifact Smith, found themselves besieged by teams from other cities. Ji Bozhai was covered in wounds, while Luo Jiaoyang and the others were in even worse shape. Qin Shangwu desperately wanted to send in replacements, but he had no Artifact Smiths available, leaving him to watch the dire situation unfold helplessly.

“Headmaster Qin, keeping Ji Bozhai in Star Yearn City is truly a waste of talent,” Zuo Ping sneered. “Why not sell him to our Newgrass City? At least we have plenty of Artifact Smiths here.”

“Ah, but your Newgrass City buildings collapse too easily. Better sell him to our Flying Blossom City. With Zheng Tiao as his partner, he’d be far more effective than those unfamiliar youngsters.”

“Your buildings are the ones that collapse! Every single one in Flying Blossom City!”

“Headmaster Qin, don’t take it too hard. After all, Star Yearn City is used to losing. One more defeat today won’t make much difference.”

What a shame such fine people had to open their mouths.

Qin Shangwu’s face turned green with rage. Who would willingly accept constant defeat? Especially when they could have won—Ji Bozhai’s Essence Power was formidable. Even after his Divine Tool was destroyed, his raw Essence Power alone could rival that of several teams using their Divine Tools. A genius like him deserved victory!

But these teams had clearly planned ahead. Unable to win fairly, they resorted to dragging out the match, ensuring Star Yearn City’s team couldn’t stand under the moonlight for the required half-hour. At their most shameless, two teams even attacked simultaneously.

Qin Shangwu clenched his fists until they turned white. If not for the rules, he would have stepped in himself.

“Star Yearn City requests a substitution—” someone announced.

Qin Shangwu turned, ready to berate whoever had made such a reckless announcement. Who did they have left to substitute?

But when he turned, he saw Mingyi standing in the arena, her face pale, the white cloth wrapped around her arm soaked through with blood. She swayed unsteadily, barely able to stand.

“Nonsense!” He rushed forward. “What are you doing here?”

“Headmaster, I need to save someone, but I can’t do it alone. So I’m here to help them win this match,” she said quickly and softly. “Once we win, I need you and them to help me!”

Seeing her so desperate was rare. Qin Shangwu nodded without thinking. “Fine.”

Only after agreeing did he laugh bitterly. “What do you think this is? You can’t just declare victory like that. Even ignoring your severe injuries, our team in there is already at their limit…”

“There’s no battle that can’t be won—only teams that don’t know how to win.” Pushing Xiuyun toward him, Mingyi strode into the Nether Domain at the center of the arena.

“What an arrogant brat!” The headmasters from various cities in the VIP seats burst into mocking laughter. “In that state, he’ll be torn apart the moment he steps into the Nether Domain.”

It was difficult to replace someone mid-competition, as newcomers entering the Nether Domain couldn’t immediately regroup with their team and risked being ambushed along the way—especially someone as frail and injured as her.

All eyes turned to her, but few held any hope. Some even instructed medics to stand by in advance.

Yet, She Tianlin was visibly excited.

When he had seen Mingyi earlier, her destroyed meridians had left her devoid of fighting spirit, her demeanor calm and resigned, exuding a sense of defeat. But now, her gaze was no different from when she had been in Sunspire City, and the aura around her was so oppressive that some spectators below found it hard to breathe.

This wasn’t Mingyi—it was Ming Xian.

He didn’t know what had provoked her, but She Tianlin was eager to see what she could do with her meridians in such a ruined state.

The moment she entered the Nether Domain, Essence Power surged toward her. Mingyi shielded herself with a pure white barrier, then raised Star River Sunset and unleashed a massive counterattack toward the source of the assault.

A deafening explosion followed as a blinding white light shot skyward, nearly piercing through the Nether Domain itself.

“Utterly foolish,” Zuo Ping scoffed. “This arena demands stealth. A spectacle like this will only draw enemies faster.”

“Not quite,” She Tianlin smiled. “Such a display won’t just attract enemies.”

A colossal white pillar of light erupted from a vast sea of flowers. Ji Bozhai whipped around at the sight and immediately barked, “Go find her!”

“Mingyi?” Luo Jiaoyang murmured, blood trickling down his half-lidded eyes. “She actually came… Couldn’t bear to watch us die here, huh?”

Without confirming or denying, Ji Bozhai cleared the path, leading them toward the light at full speed.

Pure white Essence Power was rare, let alone of such magnitude. For a moment, the other teams hesitated, wondering if Sunspire City had replaced Mingyi with Ming Xian.

But the Sunspire City contingent darkened with fury, charging toward the source of the light and launching attacks the moment they drew near.

“Traitor! Traitor!”

A barrage of multicolored Essence Power surged toward her. Mingyi flung out over a dozen defensive Divine Tools, assembling them into a shell-like barrier that encased her completely.

The attacks only dented the shell, prompting the observing elders to turn their gazes toward She Tianlin.

He met their looks with shameless defiance. “Why stare at me? I didn’t teach her that.”

He would never teach Mingyi such a cowardly Divine Tool—she had picked it up on her own.

With Yong Wang absent today, Wei Changsheng led Sunspire City’s team. His eyes burned with rage as he roared, “Crush that shell—and her—into dust!”

Assaulting a defensive Divine Tool head-on was far from wise, an effort that yielded half the result for twice the work. But driven by personal grudges, they channeled all their Essence Power into a tidal wave of attacks aimed at the shell.

Mingyi coated the exterior with a layer of pure white Essence Power. When the onslaught came, the shell was merely pushed back, remaining intact.

“Their Essence Power will take half an incense stick’s time to recover. What are you waiting for?” Mingyi’s voice, amplified by Essence Power, rang out as the shell swayed from the impact.

The Newgrass City team, lying in ambush nearby, immediately seized the opportunity and swiftly eliminated the Sunspire City members, whose lips had already turned pale with fury.

The massive waves of Essence Power they had unleashed were still attacking all around. Mingyi drew out a wisp of her own Essence Power and flung it away, diverting the calamity eastward to drown the celebrating crowd from Newgrass City.

Though ownerless Essence Power wasn’t particularly harmful, the sheer volume of it made it a persistent nuisance. The people of Newgrass City were just opening their mouths to curse her in frustration when an icy chill suddenly crept up the backs of their necks.

CONTENT END 125

chapters.title: Chapter 126
chapters.content:
Luo Jiaoyang never expected such a stroke of luck. No sooner had they arrived than they witnessed Sunspire City being eliminated by Newgrass City—and they could conveniently eliminate Newgrass City, which was now trapped in the Essence Power sea.

“Perfect timing—I’m starving. Those bastards kept targeting us. No amount of Essence Power would’ve been enough to keep up.” Fan Yao cursed under his breath before greedily devouring the surrounding Essence Power.

This method couldn’t fully convert another’s Essence Power into their own—much of it would be wasted—but it was better than nothing. They were all exhausted beyond measure.

Ji Bozhai ignored them, stepping forward on his flying sword to pull Mingyi out of the eggshell-like barrier.

“How did you suddenly—”

“Win quickly!” She gripped his hand, her eyes blazing. “Win this match, then come with me!”

“…”

He had never seen such fervor in her gaze before—her eyes, fixed on him, held nothing but his reflection.

Ji Bozhai’s heart skipped a beat, and he turned his head away uncomfortably. “Understood.”

Mingyi took the Divine Tools from their hands, swiftly repairing them while guiding their retreat.

“Her technique is too polished.” The masters in the viewing seats once again turned their gazes toward She Tianlin.

She Tianlin chuckled. “Azure Cloud never lacks talent. That kid’s got a natural gift.”

“Natural gift alone can’t explain this level of skill without proper guidance.” Zuo Ping glared at him. “Master She, don’t tell me you’ve taken on another disciple in secret.”

“What kind of man do you take me for?” She Tianlin’s expression darkened as he slammed the table and pointed to the sky. “I swore an oath—I would only ever take Ming Xian as my disciple in this lifetime!”

If only he had taken more. Just look at those repair techniques—identical to his own.

The other masters swallowed their words, stifling their frustration before turning back to the match.

What would take most Artifact Smiths hours of quiet concentration to repair, she adjusted in mere moments with a few twists of soft iron. A surge of Essence Power later, the Divine Tools gleamed as if brand new.

The Star Yearn City team, previously on the brink of collapse, now seemed revitalized, their fighting spirit renewed.

“This won’t do.” The Moonchase City team watched from the shadows, murmuring among themselves. “Take out their Artifact Smith first. She’s already injured—easier to handle than the others.”

Everyone agreed. So when the two teams crossed paths again, they prioritized attacking the Artifact Smith.

But—why was it that when others were targeted, Ji Bozhai merely blocked the attacks, yet the moment they aimed at the Artifact Smith, he turned into a wrathful deity? Not only did he shield her, but he retaliated with overwhelming Essence Power, as if intent on killing the attacker.

Fortunately, Moonchase City’s leader reacted swiftly, knocking his teammate unconscious to eliminate them before Ji Bozhai’s strike could land.

“Has he realized how crucial the Artifact Smith is?” Fan Yao muttered excitedly.

Chu He shook his head. “Or maybe it’s just because it’s Ming Guniang.”

Ridiculous. What kind of place was this? Who would still be tangled up in romantic sentiments at a time like this? Fan Yao refused to believe it.

The next moment, Ji Bozhai hoisted Mingyi onto his back and said coldly, “I hate scars more than anything. If you keep pushing yourself like this, you’ll definitely end up with one.”

Mingyi was too preoccupied with scanning their surroundings to respond, but he continued, “Fine. We’ll see if there’s any spirit medicine left when we get back.”

Fan Yao: “…”They had just been injured, with countless wounds on their bodies, yet he hadn’t mentioned searching for any spiritual herbs. Shameless!

However, with Mingyi’s presence, not only could they use their Divine Tools, but their morale had also recovered significantly. Fighting their way forward, they surprisingly managed to stand under the moonlight within the Nether Domain.

Azure Snow City was rather indifferent to worldly conflicts. Even after reaching the vicinity of the moonlight, they didn’t attack. Moonchase City still had a few survivors, but seeing Ji Bozhai’s expression that clearly said, “My people are in a hurry to leave, and so am I. Anyone who stands in our way will die,” they decided to conserve their strength and watched as the group exited the Nether Domain.

The originally one-sided situation had been reversed just like that. Mingyi didn’t idle under the moonlight either. Taking advantage of the two cities’ hesitation, she filled the area around the moonlight with trap Divine Tools, layer upon layer, from the ground to the sky.

Silver soft iron gleamed coldly under the moonlight, with faint glimpses of green poison needles hidden within.

At the main table, Bo Yuankui couldn’t hold back any longer and turned to She Tianlin, saying, “These are all your proud creations from back in the day.”

She Tianlin stroked his black-and-white hair and laughed, “Ah, really? Haha.”

Haha, my foot! What’s the deal with secretly training Artifact Smiths for Star Yearn City? Back then, you clearly swore loyalty only to Sunspire City and refused to accept students from other cities!

The elders were furious, but since the man refused to admit anything, there was nothing they could do but wait for the time to come when Star Yearn City would claim victory and leave the Nether Domain.

“Star Yearn City is truly formidable this year,” Zuo Ping sneered. “If their Artifact Smiths aren’t late next time, the rest of us might not even stand a chance.”

“Indeed, with Ji Bozhai around… Huh? Where is Lord Ji?”

Just as the post-competition sarcasm was heating up, everyone looked up to find that the Star Yearn City group had already vanished without a trace, leaving only Qin Shangwu smiling at them. “They mentioned earlier that they really needed to use the restroom. Holding it in this long must have been tough. Please wait a moment, everyone, and enjoy watching the remaining teams. Haha.”

Haha, what? All that’s left is Moonchase City and the indifferent Azure Snow City—what’s there to watch?

The elders fumed, but with She Tianlin on one side and Qin Shangwu on the other, both grinning foolishly and feigning ignorance, they got nowhere.

Ji Bozhai carried Mingyi on his back as they rushed back on a flying sword, asking along the way, “Who is that person to you?”

“I don’t know, but they might be very important.” Knowing they had already wasted too much time, Mingyi’s eyes darkened, her lips pressed tightly together, and her fingers clenched his collar tightly.

Sensing her distress, Ji Bozhai lowered his gaze. “Don’t worry. As long as they’re not completely dead, there’s always a way to save them.”

Even if it meant using Essence Power to forcibly reconstruct their meridians and heart, they could hold on until Yan Xiao arrived.

However, when they returned to the courtyard, there was nothing left—not even footprints.

Mingyi searched inside and out, her eyes suddenly lighting up. “There’s no blood.”

Ji Bozhai remarked, “Sunspire City’s people are meticulous. Maybe they took him somewhere else to kill him.”

Mingyi: “…”

Chu He elbowed Ji Bozhai’s arm and gritted his teeth. “You’re usually so good at sweet-talking women. What kind of nonsense are you spouting now?”

Ji Bozhai pushed him away impatiently and helped Mingyi sit down in a chair. Fetching some medicine, he said to her, “If he’s important to you, then as long as you’re alive, his life has value to be spared. Can’t you even understand that?”

People like them only lived because they had value, and there were others who found value in living because of them.

Mingyi gave a bitter smile and suddenly grasped his hand.

CONTENT END 126

chapters.title: Chapter 127
chapters.content:
The team from Star Yearn City rose from the lower three cities to defeat the elite forces of the other five cities. Although it was only one segment of the competition in the Divine Artifact Hall, this outcome still drew the attention of the other five cities onto these five individuals.

Apart from the universally acknowledged prowess of Ji Bozhai, Mingyi’s identity particularly piqued their curiosity. They even spent a fortune to investigate her background in Star Yearn City but gained little in return.

“Since you’re already here, why not stay a few more days?” the lord of Flying Blossom City urged them. “August is just around the corner. While autumn withers the flowers in other cities, mine alone remains in full bloom. If you stay at the Xiefang Terrace in the inner courtyard, you can witness the breathtaking sight of flowers lifting their heads at dawn every morning.”

“Ah, we’ve already stayed here for several days and seen all the wonders there are to see. In my opinion, Headmaster Qin should take everyone to visit our Newgrass City—it offers a completely different charm.”

“What charm does Newgrass City have? For scenery, our Moonchase City is the place to go.”

The group laughed while subtly competing with each other. Qin Shangwu could only sigh helplessly. “We must return to Star Yearn City to report our mission.”

“You’ve barely had a chance to get out—why rush back so soon?” they retorted, glaring at him. “What, has your city produced a few treasures you’re eager to hide away?”

Qin Shangwu was overwhelmed by their barrage of words and could only wave his hand in resignation. “I’ll go ask them. Since they were the ones who won the competition, the decision should be theirs.”

All of them bore injuries. Even with physicians specializing in treating fighters accompanying them, they still had to endure some hardship.

Ji Bozhai’s wounds weren’t severe, but whenever Qin Shangwu asked when they would return to the city, he would lazily lean against the bed and say, “The wounds hurt too much—I can’t handle the journey. Let’s wait a couple more days.”

Qin Shangwu clenched his fists. A Superior Fighter like him complaining about such minor injuries—how shameless! Meanwhile, Mingyi, despite her grave injuries, hadn’t uttered a single word of complaint.

However, Mingyi truly couldn’t endure the journey at the moment. Though she had already bought a residence here and showed no intention of returning to Star Yearn City, Qin Shangwu still wanted to persuade her. After all, if she didn’t return, the other cities would surely vie for her allegiance, and she wouldn’t have a peaceful life either.

But how to convince her? Qin Shangwu hadn’t figured it out yet. Their city lacked wealth and influence, with only the conspicuous Ji Bozhai to boast of—and even he had some unresolved grievances with her.

Just as he was fretting over this, that very night, Mingyi suddenly appeared at his doorstep, her face pale as she clutched her wound. “Headmaster.”

After days of rest, some color had finally returned to her cheeks, but now she looked deathly pale again. Startled, Qin Shangwu quickly ushered her inside and sat her down. “What’s wrong?”

After a moment of hesitation, she asked, “Facing Sun City will likely hold some competitions in August. Would Headmaster like to stop by and take a look?”

Her words implied she wanted them to go to Facing Sun City together.

Qin Shangwu was puzzled. “There are plenty of competitions in various cities lately. Why Facing Sun City in particular?”

Given her identity, shouldn’t she avoid that city?

Mingyi pressed her lips together. After a long pause, she placed a letter on the table.

The ink on the letter wasn’t even fully dry, as if it had just been written and delivered. Qin Shangwu read it carefully, and half his face darkened.

“The prestigious Sunspire City, always among the top of the Six Cities, would stoop to such threats?” He stood up angrily. “Who is this Ming An? A relative of yours?”

Mingyi gave an ambiguous response: “The Empress won’t let me go and wants to use this person to force me back to Sunspire City to die. But I don’t want to die—I like living.”

She had many questions for Ming An and also wished to settle old scores with Ji Bozhai before death. After all, they had once been very close, and she couldn’t bear the thought of him learning the truth from others later.

“If you want to go, I have no objections,” Qin Shangwu mused. “But Bo Zhai has a peculiar temperament—I can’t handle him. You’ll probably have to persuade him yourself.”

“Don’t worry, Headmaster,” Mingyi nodded. “I can convince him.”

Sunspire City offered not just more opportunities for combat but also superior Crystals and Arcane Scrolls for training. Any fighter would yearn for that city, let alone the presence of the Meng Family there.

After leaving Headmaster Qin’s room, Mingyi knocked on Ji Bozhai’s door.

Ji Bozhai was in the middle of training when the interruption came, displeased. “Who is it?”

“It’s me.”

The clear voice softened his expression. He coughed lightly, instinctively straightening his collar and flicking his sleeves into a dashing drape before replying nonchalantly, “Come in.”

Mingyi entered and sat primly on the edge of his bed, asking softly, “The benefactor you mentioned earlier—the former Empress of Star Yearn City, Meng Shi—was her maiden name Xian’er?”

Ji Bozhai froze, surprised by her sudden question. His eyes darkened slightly as he evaded, “Why?”

“If it’s her, then I’ve heard of her. She was likely a lesser daughter of the Meng Family in Sunspire City, sent there for a political marriage.” Mingyi continued, “Since she’s no longer here, would you like to return to Sunspire City to visit? Her relatives are still there.”

Ji Bozhai raised an eyebrow, his expression unreadable to Mingyi.

After a moment of silence, he chuckled and leaned back on his soft couch to study her. “You want to go back to Sunspire City to save someone?”

Mingyi’s forced smile faltered. “How did you know?”

“Tricking me into going means you want to go yourself. You’d never return to that place without reason unless you were threatened. Given recent events, they’re probably using Ming An’s life to coerce you.”

Ji Bozhai smirked. “Your Empress is quite cunning—sending Ming An to capture you. If he succeeds, he redeems himself. If he fails, he becomes a hostage. After all, you’ve never known much affection and cling to the slightest kindness. You wouldn’t abandon Ming An, who saved you twice.”

The logic was sound, but Mingyi bristled. “Who said I’ve never known affection?”

“You,” he tilted his chin up. “Only those who’ve never been loved desperately seek others’ affection, even risking their own injuries to save them—such a martyr.”

His gaze fell on the fresh blood seeping through her clothes, and his tone turned sharp. “What were you thinking, running around like this?”

Mingyi, as if her tail had been stepped on, puffed her cheeks and stood to leave, but he caught her wrist.

Ji Bozhai clicked his tongue. “You used to be so patient when you needed something from me. Now you can’t even tolerate a few extra words.”

Softening his tone, he added, “Going to Sunspire City isn’t entirely out of the question.”

Mingyi turned back to eye him.

His lazy eyes brimmed with tenderness as he gently swayed her fingertips. “Say something sweet to me, just one phrase, and I’d follow you through fire and flood.”

Mingyi: “…”

To others, his charming appearance and mesmerizing sway might have been enough to coax out any sweet words. But in her eyes, he was like a spider spreading its web, idly waiting to trap some fool for amusement.

CONTENT END 127

chapters.title: Chapter 128
chapters.content:
She might have been foolish before, but she wasn’t about to make the same mistake again.

Expressionless, Mingyi sat back down and curled her lips: “Lord Ji is the best person I’ve ever met.”

It was perfunctory, insincere, and even bordering on sarcasm.

Ji Bozhai raised an eyebrow but pressed on: “Better than Situ Ling?”

Mingyi wrinkled her face: “How old are you, and how old is he? Why do you keep competing with a child?”

“You only see him as a child?”

“What else should I see him as? A father?”

“…Don’t be so sharp-tongued.” He flicked her forehead lightly and clicked his tongue. “Women are most charming when gentle and graceful. Look at you now—covered in thorns, when before you were so inviting.”

“Before wasn’t ‘inviting’—it was being weak and easy to bully, letting anyone toy with me.” Mingyi lowered her gaze to meet his. “If I stayed like that, I’d only hold your interest for a year or two. After that, you’d have plenty of beauties to turn to, and who knows where I’d end up rotting away.”

“But now, I have money, I have my own footing—I can have any man I want. Just speaking plainly to you makes you think I’m thorny. The truth is, you’re uncomfortable because I’m not so easy to control or manipulate anymore.”

His heart sank. Ji Bozhai straightened up: “What did you say?”

She arched an eyebrow: “I said I’m not so easy to control now—”

“The line before that.”

“Just speaking plainly to you.”

“Before that.” Ji Bozhai narrowed his eyes, a faint anger simmering in his gaze. “Dared to say it but not to repeat it?”

Mingyi paused, momentarily confused, then—realizing what had angered him—suddenly flashed him a wicked smile. Meeting his eyes, she enunciated each word: “I said that now I have money, I have my own footing—I can have any man I want.”

“You!” His jaw tightened. “Women in the Azure Cloud Realm cannot remarry.”

“Oh.” Mingyi nodded. “But you and I never completed the wedding rites. How would that count as remarrying?”

“…Your household registration in Star Yearn City lists you as my concubine.”

“Even simpler—just move to another city.” She spread her hands. “Facing Sun men are strong and mighty, Flying Blossom men are romantic and passionate, Chasing Moon men are considerate and attentive, and Azure Snow men are handsome and refined—what kind couldn’t I choose?”

Her eyes brightened as she continued: “Oh right, Flying Blossom City even has an Official House—the only one in all Six Cities. Since I’m here, I might as well pay a visit.”

An uncomfortable emotion swelled in his chest. Ji Bozhai had never felt like this before—so furious he actually laughed. “You’d degrade yourself just to spite me? You really can’t let go, can you?”

“Misunderstanding, my lord.” She pursed her lips. “**By nature’s way, as long as it’s voluntary, I’ve never believed women are the ones at a disadvantage, much less call it ‘degrading.’ Other women might find it shameful, but to me, it’s no different from eating or sleeping.”

“Besides, if I seek out another man, it’s not to spite you. You and I are no longer connected. Put another way—even if I don’t seek anyone else, it’s not for your sake. It’d just mean I haven’t met someone I like enough to bother.”

Mingyi looked at him earnestly: “We’re all human. If my Essence Power can match—even surpass—most men’s, why shouldn’t I live the rest of my life as freely as they do?”

No matter who heard her words, they would find them absurd, but Ji Bozhai actually listened—and even thought she made a fair point.

If he could be promiscuous, then naturally, so could she. In terms of looks, figure, or strength, she was no less than him.

He opened his mouth but found himself at a loss for words. It was like holding a handful of sand—whether he clenched his fist or loosened his grip, the sand slipped through his fingers, utterly beyond his control.

Mingyi keenly caught the flicker of panic in his eyes.

She suddenly smiled, leaning closer to him. “My lord, do you like me?”

Ji Bozhai snapped back to his senses, glaring coldly at her. “Who would like someone as reckless and lawless as you?”

“Then why are you so angry?” Her smile deepened.

Flustered, he pushed her away, gritting his teeth. “It’s you who likes me. I would never—”

“Ah!” Mingyi let herself fall backward with his motion.

His heart lurched, and his hand shot out to catch her by the waist, pulling her back.

Their eyes met, Mingyi’s brimming with mischief.

Ji Bozhai quickly released her, turning his head away with a cold snort. “You were the one who deliberately approached me and went out of your way to please me.”

“And now that I’ve stopped, why is my lord so worked up?”

“I’m not worked up.”

“Oh, really?” Mingyi nodded and stood up. “Then my lord mustn’t dwell on today’s matter and refuse to go to Sunspire City out of spite.”

“I’ll go as soon as my injuries heal. Who would stoop to quarreling with you?”

Satisfied, Mingyi turned and left.

They were two people least suited for romance, because neither liked to admit defeat. Love was like handing over half your life at the outset—no wise fighter would do such a thing.

Still, Mingyi smirked.

She found Ji Bozhai’s reaction just now utterly amusing, as if he truly cared for her. What even invoking the Meng Family couldn’t achieve had been settled with just a few teasing words.

Before setting off, she left the deeds to her properties in Flying Blossom City with Xiuyun. “I’ll be back soon. Just wait for me here.”

Xiuyun was reluctant. “How long will you be gone?”

Mingyi thought for a moment. “If all goes well, I’ll return in a month.”

If not, she might never come back.

Empress Si Hou’s move was meant to eliminate all future threats. Mingyi had no idea what she was walking into.

Once her wounds had scabbed over, Mingyi boarded the Flying Beast Cart with Qin Shangwu.

“I’ve never been to Sunspire City before,” Luo Jiaoyang said excitedly. “Is it much bigger than our Star Yearn City? Are the streets filled with superior fighters?”

Mingyi considered the question seriously. “It is quite large, but Sunspire City is built on treacherous terrain, with the main city perched on a cliff. The land isn’t suitable for farming, and the people live in hardship.”

The others were surprised. Fan Yao asked, “Then how do the commoners survive?”

“Trade,” Mingyi replied. “They collect heavy tributes from the lower cities every year, and most of it flows into the markets for commerce.”

In other words, any city could fall from the Upper Three Cities—except Sunspire. If they lost their status, their people would suffer. That was why, even at the cost of their dignity, they had to ally with Moonchase City to maintain their position.

And the rising Star Yearn City had become a threat to their standing, one they were eager to eliminate. So before they departed, She Tianlin specially gave Mingyi a set of protective armor.

“You are the sun that will never set,” Old She said, looking at her with hopeful eyes. “Welcome back to Sunspire City.”

CONTENT END 128

chapters.title: Chapter 129
chapters.content:
However, in Sunspire City, She Tianlin was probably the only one who truly welcomed Mingyi.

The moment their beast-drawn carriage arrived at the city’s docks, it was surrounded by imperial guards. Officials from the inner court arrived with tokens to receive them, though without much enthusiasm. They merely remarked indifferently, “The competition in August is still over half a month away. You’ve arrived rather early.”

The rising sun bathed the entire city in golden light, making it hard for anyone to keep their eyes open—hence, no one bothered to retort.

Mingyi walked among them, head lowered, her face unseen by anyone.

Yet, the moment they reached the inn, she was immediately summoned by the Empress.

Recognizing the all-too-familiar messenger, Mingyi laughed after hearing his words: “Knowing full well she’s waiting to kill me, why would I be foolish enough to walk right into her hands?”

It had been a long time since they last met, and the once-obedient Ming Xian seemed like a completely different person. The messenger was taken aback but maintained his usual stern tone: “This is the Empress’s command.”

“I am now a citizen of Star Yearn City. What does your Empress’s command have to do with me? Must I obey?” She scoffed. “By protocol, I should first meet with your Minister Superior.”

“Are you threatening the Empress?” The messenger frowned.

Mingyi found this amusing: “Do you not know why I’m here?”

If not for the Empress’s threats, she would still be admiring flowers in Flying Blossom City.

Unable to argue, the messenger’s expression darkened: “The Empress decrees that if you refuse to go, Ming An will be executed in the marketplace.”

“Fine. The moment she pushes him forward, I’ll march straight into the inner court to see the Minister Superior.” Mingyi clapped her hands. “Dragging her entire family down to accompany Ming An in death—I’d say I’ve done my best.”

“You!” The messenger was furious. “Rumors of your betrayal had reached us, but I didn’t believe them—until now. You’ve grown utterly insolent!”

“The insolent one here is you.” Mingyi stood, her gaze icy. “You were the ones who always reprimanded me, trampled on my achievements, and pocketed my rewards. Yet you’re just a messenger, and she’s nothing more than a vine clinging to royal power. How dare you look down on me?”

The messenger staggered back in shock.

“For seven years, I fought tooth and nail to bring glory to Sunspire City. The Empress’s family’s wealth was built on my efforts. And you—you don’t even bow when you see me, yet you presume to lecture me on propriety every time you open your mouth. Who do you think you are?”

“You—”

“I’ve returned not to beg for their release, but to ensure that if they aren’t freed, I’ll drag you all down with me.” Mingyi clapped her hands mockingly. “After all, I don’t have much time left. Taking you all with me won’t be so lonely.”

“Madwoman! You’re insane!” Terrified, the messenger scrambled out, only to collide with Ji Bozhai.

He didn’t recognize the man, but spotting the sky-blue Mist Rain Robe of Star Yearn City, he immediately grabbed him and cried, “That woman is a lunatic, a traitor! Anyone who shelters her will meet a terrible end!”

“Oh?” Ji Bozhai smiled, plucking the horsetail whisk from the messenger’s hands. With a flick, it transformed into an icy blade pressed against his throat. “Is the madwoman you speak of as murderous as I am, who kills at the slightest provocation?”

“…”

Half an incense stick’s time later, the messenger—now unconscious from shock and rage—was carried out of the inn and loaded onto a carriage.

Qin Shangwu watched from the window before turning to the two men standing before him, puzzled. “Who did this?”

Ji Bozhai spread his hands innocently. “No.”

Mingyi nodded in agreement. “I can testify, there was indeed no physical altercation. He doesn’t even have a scratch on him.”

“Then how did a perfectly fine palace official walk in standing up and get carried out horizontally?” he frowned. “People might think Star Yearn City has no manners, acting recklessly on someone else’s turf.”

“Don’t worry, he sneaked out and won’t dare make a fuss when he returns,” Mingyi said.

Ji Bozhai nodded. “Just a nobody, Master. Not worth your concern.”

Seeing how these two were in cahoots, Qin Shangwu snorted but didn’t bother exposing them. “I’ve borrowed Sunspire City’s nearby training grounds. Their equipment is far superior to ours in Star Yearn City. Stay put and train harder these days.”

Luo Jiaoyang couldn’t resist chiming in. “Last time you said we shouldn’t boost other cities’ morale at the expense of Star Yearn’s pride. Now you’re singing their praises?”

Qin Shangwu couldn’t lay a hand on Mingyi or Ji Bozhai, but Luo Jiaoyang was fair game. A swift punch later, he grumbled, “Where the moon looks rounder depends on the heart, but these tools are tangible facts. Sunspire City has dominated for years with solid foundations. Learn humbly!”

“Yes, sir!” they chorused.

Empress Si Hou, having failed to summon Mingyi, wasn’t about to let it slide—especially after hearing how arrogantly Mingyi had threatened her. She promptly dragged the maids who once served Mingyi to the bustling market and executed them one by one.

By the time Mingyi rushed over upon hearing the news, the ground was already soaked in blood. Several maids—not particularly close to her but entirely innocent—lay decapitated, their corpses hastily wrapped and hauled away.

“What a sin. Look, one of them is still twitching,” someone nearby whispered behind their hand.

Mingyi took half a step forward when suddenly, the Nether Domain descended around her.

Looking up, she saw Empress Si Hou’s masked assassin approaching wordlessly, intent on taking her head.

A fight in the crowded market was risky, but it was also the easiest place to strike. Mingyi was poisoned; if he acted fast enough…

As the assassin closed in, he suddenly saw Mingyi sidestep, revealing a strikingly handsome face behind her.

Bringing a pretty boy to the market? —his first thought.

The next instant, the “pretty boy” had him by the throat with crushing force, plunging his vision into darkness.

“This is what you call formidable?” Ji Bozhai tossed him aside disdainfully, glancing at Mingyi.

Mingyi shrugged. “Child’s play for you, but tricky for me.”

“You invited me out for local delicacies, and this is what you meant?”

“Of course not.” Glancing at the maids’ bodies on the platform, Mingyi pressed her lips together and led him forward. “The local specialty is fried dough balls bigger than your head. Never tried them, but the inner court folks mentioned them before.”

Ji Bozhai followed, his eyes lingering on her subtly clenched hand within her sleeve. Quietly, he said, “After all she’s done to you, you’re not still holding onto some hope for her, are you?”

He didn’t specify who “she” was, but Mingyi understood.

She turned, meeting his gaze deeply, and suddenly asked, “If you were me—how would you treat this woman who was your mother for years but now wants you dead?”

With a slight pause, Ji Bozhai sneered, “You forgot, I don’t have a mother.”

CONTENT END 129

chapters.title: Chapter 130
chapters.content:
Mingyi choked slightly, lowering her eyes as she said, “Everyone has a mother. When you were born, your mother just wasn’t by your side.”

“You call someone who abandoned me after birth a mother?” Ji Bozhai scoffed. “Just a stranger at best.”

If there had been extenuating circumstances, it might have been different. But the people at the Slave Arena told him he had been left there by a group of well-dressed individuals. They had deliberately noted the location of the Slave Arena, as if intending to return for him someday.

Yet, nineteen years had passed. He waited day and night, but no one ever came looking for him.

Waiting too long for anything breeds resentment, let alone waiting for one’s parents amidst endless torment and suffering. So, by the age of ten, Ji Bozhai stopped waiting altogether. He simply assumed they were dead. If he ever discovered they were still alive, it wouldn’t matter—he no longer held any expectations, nor would he acknowledge any so-called blood ties.

If they stayed out of his way, fine. But if they proved to be as meddlesome as Mingyi’s so-called Empress, he wouldn’t show them the slightest mercy.

The woman beside him looked at him, hesitating to speak.

“What?” Ji Bozhai raised an eyebrow. “In your state, are you still trying to ‘enlighten’ me?”

“No,” Mingyi shook her head. “I just think… you’re admirable.”

Cold and decisive, utterly unburdened by sentiment.

The Empress had already tried to kill her again. Mingyi thought to herself—there was no need to show any mercy anymore. Wasn’t the Empress just afraid her true identity as a woman would be exposed, dragging her maternal family down with her?

After sharing a meal with Ji Bozhai, Mingyi deliberately returned to retrieve the flamboyant dress he had once gifted her.

With the Bright Moon Earring dangling from her ear and her slender frame wrapped in shimmering silk, she turned gracefully—once more a peerless beauty.

Ji Bozhai watched her, slightly unsettled. “Why the sudden change of attire?”

Mingyi didn’t answer directly. Instead, she said, “The inner court of Sunspire City is the place I know best. I know where the Empress’s private dungeon is. With a map, you could take advantage of the chaos in the inner court tomorrow and rescue Ming An.”

His brow twitched slightly. Ji Bozhai leaned back against a wooden pillar, arms crossed. “A risky endeavor like this offers me no benefit. Why would you think I’d help you?”

“After it’s done—” Mingyi lowered her gaze, “I’ll tell you who your birth parents are.”

The smirk on his face faded. Ji Bozhai straightened, staring at her intently.

Mingyi didn’t dare meet his eyes, busying herself with arranging the jewelry on the table. “Among the group that sent you to the Slave Arena back then, Ming An was likely one of them. Of course, this is just speculation. Only Ming An knows the full truth of what happened. If you rescue him, everything will come to light—”

Before she could finish, a hand clamped around the back of her neck.

Ji Bozhai gripped her firmly, his voice icy. “You knew who my parents were from the very beginning. Is that why you approached me?”

Mingyi remained silent.

Outside the window, the sun dipped below the horizon, casting a golden glow through the lattice and into the inn’s room. It should have been a warm scene, but an oppressive, murderous aura slowly filled the space, making it hard to breathe.

Ji Bozhai couldn’t accept that something so monumental had been revealed so casually, as if she had set a trap for him from the start.

Recalling all the kindness she had shown him before, he smirked humorlessly. “You wouldn’t happen to owe me some great debt, would you? Here to repay it before you die?”

Her eyelashes fluttered slightly as Mingyi gave a bitter smile. “Even at death’s door, I still have a conscience. Instead of praising me, you look like you want to kill me. Lord Ji, surely you’re not still hung up on matters of sincerity?”

His heart sank abruptly, and Ji Bozhai’s hand on the nape of her neck trembled slightly.

Indeed, Ming Xian, the esteemed heir of the Ming family in Sunspire City—even if he had fallen into dire straits, he should have had plenty of options once he recovered. The only reason he had entered the inner court as a Dancing Girl was to get close to him.

What kind of debt could he possibly owe to willingly degrade himself like this just to be by his side? A blood feud? The murder of his mother?

As unease grew in his heart, Ji Bozhai’s voice turned icy. “I despise being played for a fool.”

“Your Lordship is peerlessly brilliant—how could you ever be a fool?” Patting the hand resting on her neck, Mingyi chuckled softly. “Even without your intervention, I won’t live much longer. Why rush things now?”

Ji Bozhai suddenly calmed down.

He studied the reflection in the bronze mirror carefully.

She was composed, serene—her eyes dull.

Yes, she believed her time was short, which was why she cared so little.

But what if she lived longer? Would she still remain so indifferent when faced with certain things?

Withdrawing his hand, Ji Bozhai took a deep breath. “Give me the map.”

Mingyi rose to fetch paper and brush, sketching out the map for him.

Sunspire City was truly a place she had poured her heart and soul into. The map of the inner court was meticulously detailed—every stone pillar, every lantern, every dog, and even every cracked tile was marked.

Ji Bozhai took the map and fixed his gaze on her. “Will there be danger tomorrow?”

“Yes.” Mingyi lowered her eyes. “But it has nothing to do with you. If I’m lucky, I might return to Flying Blossom City. If not, I’d trouble you to pass a message to Xiuyun—tell her I still prefer Sunspire City, and that she should live well in Flying Blossom.”

“Nothing to say to me?” He raised an eyebrow.

Mingyi paused briefly before meeting his gaze. “I hope Your Lordship remains forever free, never becoming a tool in someone else’s hands.”

It sounded like a blessing—yet also like advice from one who had learned the hard way.

Ji Bozhai snorted coldly, clutching the map as he turned to leave.

Naturally, he would never become someone else’s tool. In this world, everyone else was merely an instrument for his vengeance.

The last traces of twilight vanished from the horizon. Mingyi spent the entire night preparing meticulously. Early the next morning, as Qin Shangwu stepped outside, he saw Mingyi already waiting, bowing to him. “Master.”

Startled by her attire, Qin Shangwu frowned. “You—”

“Today is about meeting an old acquaintance. Master, please indulge her,” Ji Bozhai said as he emerged from behind, bowing to Qin Shangwu in passing.

Luo Jiaoyang and the others, ever eager for drama, immediately crowded around Mingyi. “Won’t they recognize you like this?”

“Even if they notice, they wouldn’t dare acknowledge it. Ming Xian was a man, after all.”

“How amusing. I’d love to see the reactions of those Sunspire City folk.”

Qin Shangwu was reluctant to stir trouble—this was Sunspire City’s territory, and causing a scene might make their return difficult. But when he glanced at Ji Bozhai, his usually prudent disciple showed no concern. Perhaps he already had a contingency plan.

Mingyi had helped them greatly. If she had a wish to fulfill, Qin Shangwu hesitated for a moment before deciding to turn a blind eye.

In the Azure Cloud Realm, women held lowly status. Even in the prosperous and enlightened Sunspire City, women were only fit to be maids or bear children. Even Empress Si Hou had to use the side gates when entering or leaving the inner courtyard.

Yet today, the hem of a crimson skirt brushed against the threshold of the inner courtyard’s main gate.

CONTENT END 130

chapters.title: Chapter 131
chapters.content:
The guards holding the Golden Crow Halberds at the gate couldn’t help but frown at the approaching figure. With hair dark as clouds and features delicate as the moon, the girl was as tender as a newly bloomed flower. Anywhere else, she would surely have drawn a crowd of admirers.

But this was the main gate of Sunspire City—what place did a woman have here? After a moment’s hesitation, they blocked the group’s path.

“Female attendants must enter through the eastern side gate.”

“I’ve walked through this gate for nineteen years, and this is the first time anyone’s told me to use a side entrance.” Mingyi smiled faintly, lifting her gaze to them. “Though it’s only been half a year, your eyesight seems to have worsened considerably.”

The guards froze, studying her carefully before their expressions changed. “Your Highness?”

The guard captain rushed over, slapping their helmets angrily. “What ‘Highness’? Ming Xian is dead—the inner court has already held the mourning rites. The only remaining prince is Yong Wang—do you not recognize him? How dare you address a woman as ‘Highness’? This is a grave offense!”

With that, he glanced at their group and declared, “Women are not permitted through the main gate. Move along.”

This captain was one of Empress Si Hou’s people, so his obstruction was no surprise. Mingyi checked the time, then turned just as Yong Wang’s entourage approached.

“How bold of you to block honored guests from Star Yearn City,” Dan Er said from Yong Wang’s side, eyeing Mingyi with amusement. “Don’t let them think Sunspire City lacks hospitality.”

“There is no precedent for women entering through the main gate,” the captain said stiffly, his face pale. “I guard this post, and I must uphold its rules.”

“Oh, but there is precedent.” Dan Er grinned wider, pointing at Mingyi. “She’s walked through this gate at least eight hundred times, if not a thousand. If you think the rules are broken, why not accompany us to see Minister Superior Da Si?”

As the captain hesitated, Yong Wang’s lieutenant stepped forward to confront the guards. Seizing the moment, Dan Er gestured to Mingyi. “After you.”

If anyone wanted Mingyi to enter the inner court most, it was Yong Wang and the Meng clan. They had been waiting here since receiving word, and the inner court was already packed with spectators eager to witness the spectacle.

Ming Li, Minister Superior of Sunspire City, was puzzled by the unusually early arrivals when Empress Si Hou suddenly rushed in, weeping. She knelt beside him and pleaded, “I beg Minister Superior to grant me justice!”

With so many eyes watching, Ming Li hesitated. “This is hardly the place. Whatever it is, it can wait until after we’ve received Sunspire City’s guests.”

By then, it would be too late. The Empress clenched her teeth.

She never imagined Mingyi would dare to stride into the inner court in a Hairpin Skirt, flaunting her defiance. The guards had failed to stop her, and if she didn’t plead her case now, she’d lose her chance to speak.

This Mingyi—after just one trip outside, she’d transformed into someone bold enough to defy her!

Taking a deep breath, the Empress hurriedly said, “Yesterday, a foolish maid of mine mistakenly took a bowl of bird’s nest meant for Meng Guifei. I thought it a trivial matter and sent someone to apologize, but who knew my sister would hold a grudge? She vowed to make me pay today. With the arrival of fighters from another city, I feared such petty quarrels might disrupt your important affairs, so I came to speak first.”

Since when were harem squabbles worth bringing here? Ming Li glared at her. “You’ve always been composed—what’s gotten into you today—”

“Minister Superior, the Fighters from Star Yearn City have arrived.”

With no time to reprimand Consort Si further, Ming Li turned his gaze toward the entrance.

A single glance froze him in place.

Qin Shangwu entered with five fighters in tow. Ji Bozhai, Luo Jiaoyang, and the others—they had gathered information on their distinguishing features and naturally recognized them. But… the fighter walking in the center was actually a woman?

Her embroidered skirt trailed along the ground, hair ornaments swaying gently as she followed her mentor into the hall. Under the scrutiny of countless eyes, she performed a woman’s curtsy: “Greetings to the Minister Superior of Facing Sun.”

The entire hall fell silent. Not a single voice could be heard. The gazes directed at her ranged from astonishment to disgust and even mockery.

Truly, Star Yearn City lived up to its reputation as one of the lower three cities—utterly ignorant of propriety. To bring a woman to such a grand occasion!

She Tianlin, seated closest to the Minister Superior, only had to tilt his head to see the disbelief in the latter’s eyes.

“Young lady…” Ming Li rose to his feet. “Whose family do you belong to?”

Mingyi took two steps forward, raising her hand to her forehead. “This humble girl bears the surname Ming.”

Ming?

Ming was indeed a prominent surname, but could it really be such a coincidence? To resemble Ming Xian so strikingly in features and also share the same surname?

Ming Li studied her for a long moment before suddenly turning to Consort Si with a laugh. “If not for Star Yearn City’s people, I’d truly think you’d secretly borne me a daughter.”

Consort Si’s face turned ashen, her head remaining bowed.

Mingyi lowered her saluting hand and lifted her gaze to meet his. “This humble girl is not from Star Yearn City. She was born in Sunspire City.”

Ming Li sensed something amiss and narrowed his eyes slightly. “Where in Sunspire City?”

“The inner palace grounds—Zhaoyang Palace.”

The crowd erupted in murmurs, all eyes shifting to Consort Si.

Zhaoyang Palace—the residence of Consort Yan Si.

Consort Yan’s fingers trembled. After a deep breath, she lifted her head with a cold expression and snapped, “What sorceress dares spout such nonsense! Is this how Star Yearn City presents itself before the Minister Superior of Facing Sun?”

Qin Shangwu clasped his hands in apology. “Consort Si, please forgive us. Mingyi—or rather, Ming Xian—has shed blood and sweat for your Sunspire City. Now gravely injured and repeatedly hunted down, she had no choice but to follow us into these inner halls today. Star Yearn City owes her a debt; this is merely a small favor in return.”

The moment the name Ming Xian was uttered, the murmurs swelled into an uproar. Some even leaped to their feet in outrage, shouting, “Ming Xian is a man—the heir of Sunspire City! What vile scheme is this, presenting a woman as his impostor!”

“Exactly! Ming Xian is already dead. The inner palace held funeral rites not long ago—we’re still observing mourning, abstaining from meat and music!”

“Ming Xian is dead?” Dan Er asked with a smile. “Does the coffin enshrined in the inner palace contain a corpse?”

“Dan Er, how dare you!” Consort Yan roared. “The heir of Sunspire City—do you presume to open his coffin for inspection?”

“I believe it is Consort Si who presumes too much.” Meng Guifei arrived belatedly, entering through a side door and gliding gracefully toward the seat beside the Minister Superior.

Ming Li frowned at her. “At a time like this, surely you’re not here to vie for favor.”

“Minister Superior, be assured this humble consort seeks only to prevent your deception, not to compete for affection.” Meng Guifei saluted him, then pointed a vermilion-tipped finger at Mingyi. “She is Ming Xian. Ming Xian has been a woman since birth. It was Consort Si who deliberately deceived the Minister Superior, repeatedly blocking physicians from examining her, orchestrating this grand deception that led to today’s predicament!”

The inner palace of Sunspire City erupted into chaos as nobles and ministers broke into heated arguments.

How could Ming Xian be a girl? She had been designated as the heir from birth because of her Crimson Meridians. If she were a girl…

If she were a girl, even with the Crimson Meridians, she wouldn’t be taken seriously.

CONTENT END 131

chapters.title: Chapter 132
chapters.content:
Empress Yan was furious, but Consort Meng had come fully prepared. With a wave of her hand, she summoned several witnesses—physicians and palace attendants—who all testified in unison that the Empress had never allowed anyone near Ming Xian.

The Empress stubbornly denied the accusations, and the hall erupted into chaos.

“Enough!” Ming Li suddenly slammed his hand on the golden throne with a thunderous crash, instantly silencing the court.

Taking a few ragged breaths, his trembling finger pointed at Mingyi. “You—explain what happened.”

Mingyi bowed her head slightly. “I was raised as a boy since childhood. Even if I were truly a woman, I have undeniably secured Sunspire City’s victory in the tournament for seven consecutive years. Without me, Sunspire City would not be where it is today.”

Her words immediately drew discontent from Wei Changsheng and others nearby, who sneered, “Without you? You’re just a little stronger in Essence Power. But did you win the championship alone? Are the rest of us worthless?”

Mingyi glanced at them and chuckled. “I could still win the championship in any other city. But you? Without me, you’re all useless. How dare you even speak?”

Wei Changsheng, enraged, slammed the table. “Who are you calling useless?!”

“Whoever needs rescuing every year at the Six Cities Tournament is useless,” she said disdainfully. “Did you really think you got into the Academicians’ Court on your own merit?”

The Wei family had close ties with the Yan family, and it was only through Empress Yan’s influence that Wei Changsheng had been forced into the Academicians’ Court, with orders for her to support him. Over the years, Mingyi had grown accustomed to carrying four mediocre fighters to victory. Yet now, those very same mediocre fighters actually believed they were the reason for their success.

Wei Changsheng’s face flushed crimson, but after their humiliating defeat in Flying Blossom City, he had no ground to retort.

Turning her gaze back to the Minister Superior, Mingyi continued, “If not for Consort Meng, this secret might have remained hidden forever, and I would have remained Sunspire City’s tool for victory. But unfortunately, Consort Meng was too eager to overthrow Empress Yan. She investigated for four years and finally found a crack—she discovered my true identity.”

“Knowing it was one thing. Empress Yan was cunning enough to ensure no one could verify my body. But fate had other plans. I was not her biological child, and I was born with Crimson Meridians. She was desperate to control me, so from the age of ten, she fed me ‘Sky of Eternal Regret,’ giving me the antidote each month to keep me in her grip.”

“‘Sky of Eternal Regret’ is a poison she specially commissioned to control Fighters.” Mingyi’s eyes narrowed as she turned to the Empress. “Now, I have a question for Empress Yan. Do you know where this poison was developed?”

Empress Yan’s face turned ashen. “You vile witch, spouting nonsense—”

“It was developed in a Slave Arena in Star Yearn City,” Mingyi continued calmly. “Tested on living slaves. Out of countless lives, only one child survived.”

Ji Bozhai’s fingers twitched at his side. Frowning, he looked toward the Empress on the throne.

The Empress, however, paid no mind to such trivial matters, frantically defending herself instead. “Minister Superior, I knew nothing of this!”

“Let her finish,” Ming Li said coldly.

Mingyi nodded and turned back to Consort Meng. “Your Highness must have also discovered where Empress Yan hid the antidotes, which is why you seized the chance to burn the entire courtyard to ashes. Without the antidote, my meridians were ravaged by the poison. And Empress Yan, without hesitation, ordered her people to execute me—lest Consort Meng use the opportunity to verify my identity and expose her.”The ministers erupted in uproar: “How—how can this warrant execution?”

“Ming Xian was the hope of our Sunspire City, even if she’s a woman… alas.”

“Didn’t you hear? Poison destroyed her meridians—she’s not as formidable as before. That’s why Consort Si discarded her.”

“But after raising her for so many years, even if not by blood, shouldn’t there be affection? How could she be so heartless?”

“Exactly…”

Amid the murmurs, Ming Li seized Yan Si Hou’s wrist and demanded angrily, “Ming Xian isn’t your biological child?”

Yan Si Hou panicked: “She—she is still a child of my clan. Our bloodline is naturally gifted.”

“Then why abandon your own child?” Ming Li’s voice darkened with fury. “If you could discard your own flesh and blood, others must mean nothing to you.”

“No, it’s not like that, Minister Superior! This concubine reveres you—I never intended to deceive you!” Yan Si Hou fell to her knees, tears streaming. “Back then, you desperately wanted a child with Crimson Meridians to revitalize Sunspire City. Naturally, I wanted to share your burden. But the child I bore after ten months… didn’t have crimson meridians. With everyone’s expectations weighing on us, how could I bear to disappoint you? So I took a newborn from my clan who had the crimson meridians.”

“She is still a child of my clan, and she brought glory to Sunspire City. Minister Superior—”

“Then where is our real child?” Ming Li’s eyes burned as he glared at her. “Did you kill them?”

“No! I didn’t deliberately kill them!” Yan Si Hou shook her head frantically. “I was just too flustered and busy at the time and neglected them. By the time I remembered, the eunuchs had already taken them away in the chaos. I don’t know where they went.”

“You don’t know?” Ming Li laughed bitterly. “Your eunuchs, the people you sent away—and you claim you don’t know where they are?”

Yan Si Hou wept openly. “This concubine truly doesn’t know.”

She couldn’t have deliberately harmed her own child. But with the crimson-meridian child to care for and the need to conceal her gender, she simply had no time to spare. Later, whether out of guilt or something else, she never inquired further—knowing would only give others leverage, with no benefit to herself.

That child… was probably dead by now.

The hall was spellbound, even the guards slackening their vigilance. Seeing his chance, Ji Bozhai excused himself under the pretense of freshening up and slipped out through a side door.

Mingyi wasn’t the biological child of Sunspire City’s Empress—no wonder the Empress had been so cruel to her. Now, Ji Bozhai was deeply curious about the role Ming An had played in all this.

…

“Ming An was my most trusted eunuch. The Minister Superior also trusted him, which is why he bestowed upon him the Ming family name,” Yan Si Hou continued to sob. “But I never imagined he would betray me, letting that witch escape and bringing shame upon Sunspire City today.”

She Tianlin could bear no more and scoffed coldly: “So according to Consort Si, you committed no wrong in swapping the children—the fault lies with the eunuch who didn’t kill Ming Xian, with Consort Meng for exposing the truth, and with Mingyi for daring to return here?”

Yan Si Hou gritted her teeth. “I only sought to uphold my family’s honor and share the Minister Superior’s burdens! What wrong have I committed?”

“To taint the inner court’s bloodline is a grave crime!” Ming Li slammed the table and stood up. “You poisonous woman! Had I known you were so audacious and wicked, even if your bloodline could bring glory to Facing Sun, I should never have welcomed you into the inner court!”

“A-Li, we’ve been husband and wife for so many years, sharing the same bed through honor and disgrace. How can you abandon me just for this one mistake?” She sobbed, tears streaming down her face.

CONTENT END 132

chapters.title: Chapter 133
chapters.content:
Mingyi watched coldly, thinking that Yan Si Hou was truly desperate, willing to play the emotional card with anyone—how could she say such words to Da Si of Sunspire City?

Da Si of Sunspire City was the kind of man who prioritized profit over sentiment. From the beginning, he had married her solely for her bloodline. Since her bloodline failed to produce a child born with Crimson Meridians, he would naturally feel deceived.

For a common-born woman, ascending to the position of Si Hou was an arduous feat. Mingyi, who had stirred the Six Cities with her birth, had given Yan Shi her greatest leverage. The honors she had won over the years had further solidified her position as Empress. Yet now, the way Yan Si Hou looked at Mingyi was filled with hatred.

“Since you were exposed by Meng Guifei and forced to leave Sunspire, why did you return?” she demanded bitterly.

Mingyi spread her hands. “You know I’m not one to hold grudges. If Consort Si hadn’t relentlessly pursued me, hunting me down at every turn, I might not be here today. As you said, I’m poisoned and don’t have much time left—I just wanted to live out my remaining days in peace. But since you feared being manipulated by Meng Guifei and sought to kill me for your own security, I had no choice but to find a way to protect myself.”

Meng Guifei covered her lips with a delicate laugh. “Sister just asked Da Si to remember the affection of all these years as husband and wife, yet how could you be so ruthless as to plot the murder of the very child you raised? If one day Da Si were to stand in your way, would you move against him as well?”

The words were venomous. Everyone knew Da Si was her entire world—how could he ever stand in her way? Yet the moment she said it, Da Si’s expression darkened.

In truth, Mingyi’s actions would only lead to her demotion. After all, she had contributed greatly to Sunspire’s victories over the years. Merit and fault would balance out—she would lose her position as Si Hou, but a life of comfort was still within reach. Yet with Meng Guifei’s words, given Da Si’s temperament, it would be difficult for Yan Shi to remain.

Yan Si Hou’s eyes reddened. Staggering forward a few steps, she gazed at Mingyi before suddenly bursting into tears. “I gave you a noble status, urged you day and night to train without the slightest negligence, and made you bring glory to Sunspire City and to Da Si—all because I knew our Yan Shi clan bore a heaven-sent duty to uphold a wise ruler and unite Azure Cloud!”

“Though you are not my child, you are still a child of the Yan Shi clan. We are all subjects of the Minister Superior. What madness has possessed you today, to stand before this crowd and argue over bloodline?”

Mingyi raised a brow, but before she could retort, Yan Si Hou turned and knelt before the Minister Superior, her still-graceful face streaked with tears. “This humble consort was momentarily foolish, acting solely out of concern for the Minister Superior, and allowed a mere woman to disrupt the royal hierarchy. I am guilty! But Minister Superior, I harbor no trace of defiance. Using poison to control her was only because I feared her Essence Power was too strong, that she might one day pose a threat to you. My sincerity over all these years—you know it well.”

“Moreover, though Ming Xian is a woman, she has indisputably won the Six Cities Tournament year after year. Sunspire is brimming with talent—even a woman could surpass all the fighters from the other five cities. In my eyes, this is no disgrace, but the highest honor!”

Yan Si Hou was eloquent, a skill that had long secured her place in the inner court. Hearing her words now, even Mingyi nearly believed them. Indeed, what was wrong with securing a child born with Crimson Meridians for Sunspire? Even if it was a daughter, hadn’t she claimed victory for seven years straight?

Da Si’s expression softened slightly. Seeing the situation turning unfavorable, Meng Guifei immediately interjected, “Although the Yan Shi clan produces many superior fighters, Yan Shi women can only bear one child in their lifetime. Sister has already abandoned her own biological child, meaning she is no different from common women outside. How dare she continue to shamelessly occupy the position of Empress?”

“Though Ming Xian is formidable, he is not Sister’s biological child. If Sister truly cared for the Minister Superior, shouldn’t she let his birth parents enjoy this wealth?”

At this, Da Si also recalled, “Who are his birth parents?”

Si Hou pressed her lips together, her face grim. “They were sent by the clan. I don’t know.”

Mingyi lowered her eyes and suddenly bluffed, “If you didn’t know, why would you suddenly imprison Ming An?”

Si Hou looked at her in shock, then quickly realized, “Are you saying Ming An is your father?!”

This reaction was unexpected to Mingyi. The Empress seemed genuinely surprised, as if she truly hadn’t known.

Had her bluff failed? Mingyi fell silent.

Si Hou knelt on the floor, stunned for a long moment before her expression darkened. “No wonder… no wonder he repeatedly spared your life. So there was such a connection.”

“Sister, stop pretending.” Meng Guifei covered her lips with a sleeve. “How could you not know whose child it was when your own attendants brought it to you?”

“How could I have known?” Yan Si Hou gritted her teeth. “The entire clan hoped I would bear a child with Crimson Meridians. If I could deliver one naturally, that would be ideal. If not, they had prepared a newborn for replacement. I was in such agony during childbirth—how could I know whose child they brought?”

After panting heavily for a moment, her eyes darted about, her lips pale. “So it was Ming An… He served me faithfully for years. I never thought he would betray me too.”

“Your Majesty shows no mercy toward the child you raised for years or the loyal servant who served you for decades. No wonder everyone betrays you.” Mingyi gazed at her with pity and hatred. “After all these years, even a dog would have earned some affection. Yet you remain ruthlessly decisive, administering meridian-destroying poison without hesitation.”

“How could I rest easy without the poison?!” Yan Si Hou clenched her fists. “As this wretch said, we Yan Shi women can only bear one child. Mine is already gone, while you grow stronger by the day. If you ever reunite with your birth parents, where would that leave me?”

Her throat tight, Mingyi pinched her fingers. “I always revered you as my mother. Even though you were cold and harsh, I practiced diligently day after day to please you. Yes, I was born with gifts other children lacked—but I lacked what others had.”

No love, no trust. All she had were endless tasks and demands—a born tool.

“If it were your own child,” Mingyi asked, “would you still feed them ‘Sky of Eternal Regret’?”

Noticing the fleeting vulnerability in her eyes, Yan Si Hou suddenly seemed to gain the upper hand. She lifted her chin disdainfully. “If my own child had been born with Crimson Meridians, none of this would have happened. I would have cherished and loved them—never poison; not even cold broth would touch their lips. These are things a traitor like you could never obtain!”

Mingyi lowered her eyes and gave a faint smile. “So karma truly exists in this world after all.”

CONTENT END 133

chapters.title: Chapter 134
chapters.content:
“What do you mean by that?” Empress Yan Si Hou frowned, feeling inexplicably unsettled.

“As I mentioned to Your Majesty earlier, the poison Sky of Eternal Regret was developed in a slave arena in Star Yearn City. Among the batch of slaves tested with it, only one survived.”

Mingyi smiled. “Guess why he survived?”

Sky of Eternal Regret was a poison specifically targeting Fighters. Only those with exceptionally strong meridians could withstand it, yet people with such strong meridians would never end up in a slave arena.

The Empress was momentarily bewildered before her expression turned stern again. “Why should I guess? They’re just slaves. What difference does it make if one survived?”

Several people from Star Yearn City listening behind them grew displeased. Luo Jiaoyang immediately retorted, “What’s wrong with slave arenas? Ji Bozhai came from one. Can any of you defeat him in single combat now?”

Chu He beside him tried to cover his mouth but was too late. At these words, everyone in the hall froze.

Many had investigated Ji Bozhai’s origins, so this wasn’t surprising. But mentioning it in this context carried subtle implications.

Indeed, why would someone with meridians as strong as Ji Bozhai’s end up in a slave arena?

…

Ji Bozhai helped Ming An onto the beast-drawn carriage to Star Yearn City, noticing the man’s stiff posture.

“Are you uncomfortable somewhere?” he asked.

Ming An replied awkwardly, “No, thank you, Lord Ji.”

After walking a few steps, Ji Bozhai suddenly sensed something amiss. “This should be our first meeting. How do you know my surname?”

Ming An paused, surprised. “Didn’t Mingyi… tell you anything?”

“Tell me what?” Ji Bozhai was puzzled.

Ming An fell silent, shaking his head before asking, “Where is Mingyi now?”

“In the main hall of Sunspire City’s inner court.”

Ming An halted mid-step, hesitating before looking at him. “Let’s go there too.”

Ji Bozhai frowned. “Are you sure?”

After finally rescuing him, why return to that place?

Ming An nodded firmly, sighing with a smile. “Though the Yan clan wronged me, they’re still my late wife’s maternal family. I promised her I wouldn’t let her kin suffer.”

By the time he escaped, Empress Yan Si Hou was nearly convicted. What could returning now possibly change? Ji Bozhai was skeptical but said nothing, turning direction to escort him toward the hall.

En route, Ming An suddenly said, “Mingyi never intended to harm you. She even feels she robbed you of the wealth you deserved and owes you. But she owes you nothing—the true culprits are me and Empress Yan Si Hou.”

From the earlier conversation in the hall, Ji Bozhai had guessed this involved him. Yet hearing it from Ming An still shocked him, his grip unconsciously tightening.

“Are Mingyi and I blood-related?”

“No.” Ming An shook his head. “Mingyi is my child. Though my late wife and Empress Yan share the same clan, their ancestral ties extend beyond five generations.”

Ji Bozhai relaxed, chuckling lazily. “Then there’s nothing to discuss.”

Ming An: ?

How could this be his reaction? Wasn’t the crucial point his origins? After years of displacement, how could he show no curiosity about his own background?

“I should have died at fifteen, but a family saved me. In my eyes, they are my true family. As for who my birth mother or father is, I don’t care.” Noticing his gaze, Ji Bozhai spoke coolly, “What you plan to do today has nothing to do with me. I only want to leave Sunspire City safely with my people.”

It had to be said, his temperament was strikingly similar to Yan Si Hou—caring only about what mattered to him, indifferent to everything else, even blood ties.

Ming An studied him deeply, lips pressed tightly together.

The atmosphere in the grand hall was tense. As Ji Bozhai stepped alone through the side door, he suddenly felt countless eyes fixated on him.

Puzzled, he looked up at Mingyi, only to see her quickly avert her gaze.

Why the guilt?

Raising his eyes further, he met the scrutinizing gaze of Da Si on the throne—deep, filled with joy, yet tinged with unmistakable sorrow.

“What?” he asked.

Luo Jiaoyang tugged at his sleeve, signaling him to look to the side.

Ji Bozhai turned his head and came face-to-face with Yan Si Hou’s ecstatic, almost frenzied expression.

From a distance, the resemblance had been unclear, but up close, it was undeniable—their features shared a striking likeness, from the sharp brows to the straight nose and thin lips.

If there had been any doubt before, Ji Bozhai’s appearance now sent the onlookers into a frenzy.

“It’s uncanny! They look exactly alike!”

“Ji Bozhai is actually one of us from Sunspire?!”

“The Yan bloodline is truly formidable. He’s already so powerful—even Moonchase City lost to him in Flying Blossom City!”

“Truly, a blessing in disguise!”

Yan Si Hou, overwhelmed, seized his arm. “You’re my son? But your meridians—”

She flipped his wrist, revealing the crimson veins winding beneath his skin.

“My meridians only manifested when I was ten,” Ji Bozhai replied coldly, a stark contrast to her exhilaration. “I wasn’t born with Crimson Meridians, nor did I rely on Sunspire’s nurturing.”

“What do you mean by that? You are my child, my blood.” Yan Si Hou instinctively glared at him, but remembering their estrangement, she softened her tone. “Ah, when you were born, your meridians weren’t visible, so they appeared later.”

She turned and knelt before Da Si. “This proves that the Yan bloodline can help the Minister Superior fulfill his long-cherished wish!”

Ming Li, his earlier anger replaced by delight, waved a hand dismissively. “All this fuss over a simple case of mistaken identity. Though Ming Xian is a woman, she has brought Sunspire victory for seven years. Her contributions more than make up for the deception.”

“Minister Superior!” Meng Guifei protested urgently. Just moments ago, he had been ready to condemn the Yan clan—how could he change his mind so abruptly?

But Da Si ignored her, merely gesturing for silence. “Enough.”

He then turned a benevolent gaze toward Ji Bozhai. “I’ve long heard of this fighter’s prowess. To think he carries Sunspire’s blood! In that case—”

“Minister Superior, wait!” Meng Guifei stood abruptly. “Are we to hastily declare this Superior Fighter a royal descendant based solely on Ming Xian’s words and a passing resemblance? Isn’t this too reckless?”

Everyone present could see that this was clearly Empress Yan Si Hou desperately trying to find an escape route. How could it be such a coincidence that the child she abandoned could survive until now and even become a Superior fighter?

“The Yan clan is deceiving the emperor and coveting fame and fortune, attempting to disrupt the royal bloodline. I implore the Minister Superior to administer proper punishment!” Meng Guifei glared at the Empress before turning to Mingyi. “And you’re just speaking nonsense. Just because a skilled fighter emerged from the Slave Arena, does that necessarily mean they’re Empress Yan Si Hou’s child?”

CONTENT END 134

chapters.title: Chapter 135
chapters.content:
Mingyi felt inexplicably wronged: “I had barely begun when everyone rushed to speak upon seeing Lord Ji’s face—how is that my fault? Did I explicitly state that Lord Ji had any connection with Empress Yan?”

“Then you—”

“When I left Sunspire City years ago, someone told me I wasn’t Empress Yan’s biological child,” Mingyi said calmly. “They also said I should seek out Ji Bozhai, that he could save me—even help me return to Sunspire City.”

“With those two statements together, it was hard not to draw certain conclusions, especially after seeing Lord Ji’s face. That suspicion only grew stronger.” Mingyi chuckled lightly. “But at the time, it was merely speculation. Bringing it up today was only to await Empress Yan’s explanation.”

“What explanation should I give? I was kept in the dark too!” Empress Yan spat bitterly. “I didn’t know where the child I bore was sent—”

“How dare Your Majesty claim ignorance?” A voice interjected from the side door, laced with amusement.

Everyone turned to see Ming An, battered and bruised, clutching his arm as he limped into the grand hall.

“Greetings, Minister Superior,” he knelt, bowing slowly.

Mingyi’s pupils contracted. Instinctively, she took two steps forward and whispered, “You were tortured?”

Ming An gave a pained smile. “Falling into Empress Yan’s hands, how could one emerge unscathed? Minor injuries—pay them no mind.”

He turned to the Minister Superior, cupping his hands respectfully. “When Empress Yan was eight months pregnant, she was scouring the land for infants with Crimson Meridians. Coincidentally, my late wife had just given birth to such a child. When her clan elders learned of it, they immediately sent her to Empress Yan’s palace.”

“I told the clan leader it was a girl. But he said Crimson Meridians were rare—if it were a girl, she’d have no future. But if she could become Empress Yan’s son, she’d live a life of luxury.” Ming An sighed. “My late wife adored her maternal clan. Without hesitation, she handed over the child and even urged me to stay silent, to never acknowledge her.”
